questions.prompt: Rina ___ to school by bicycle every weekday.
questions.explanation: Rina is a singular third-person subject. In an affirmative simple-present clause, go becomes goes.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a correct simple-present negative?
questions.explanation: After does not, use the base verb like. Does already carries the third-person agreement.

questions.prompt: The books on the shelf ___ useful for our project.
questions.explanation: The subject is books, which is plural. The prepositional phrase on the shelf does not change the subject; use are.

questions.prompt: Each of the students ___ a reading journal.
questions.explanation: Each is the singular head of the subject. In the simple present, use keeps, even though students inside the of-phrase is plural.

choices: Does Sinta studies English every day?
Do Sinta study English every day?
Does Sinta study English every day?
Sinta does studies English every day?
questions.explanation: For a simple-present question with singular Sinta, use Does + subject + base verb study.
